newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran court fighting West influence holds youth.
newsitem.headline: Iran court fighting West influence holds youth.

text.p: Iranian courts set up to fight Western cutural influences have ordered 130 youths held for attending parties that were "gatherings of debauchery", a court official was quoted as saying in a newspaper on Wednesday.

The daily Resalat quoted Mohammad Kazemi, head of the Martyr Qoddusi Judicial Complex in Tehran, as saying the youths were arrested at several "gatherings of debauchery held under the pretence of being birthday parties" late last week in Tehran.
Iran's Islamic laws restrict contacts between unmarried people of different sexes who are not relatives.

Agents also seized 1,243 satellite receivers imported from Dubai from two persons who were fined 80 million rials ($27,000), Kazemi said. Iran banned satellite television in 1995 to fight a Western "cultural invasion".

Kazemi, reporting on the court's activity in the past two months, said police also arrested dozens of men and women for setting up "pleasure houses" in Tehran and seized large amounts of cash and pornography from them.
Other seizures included 10,000 litres of alcohol from an illegal plant in addition to 8,300 litres from other sources, he said. Alcohol is banned in Iran.

The court complex was set up in October 1995 in response to a call by supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei to step up the fight against "Western cultural invasion", Iran's term for the spread of Western behaviour and culture deemed to be un-Islamic. ($1 = 3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
